mechanism_narrative: A 2% quarterly increase in Real GDP (GDPC1) indicates strengthening economic demand, leading to increased consumer spending and, subsequently, higher S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 50% of quarters with 2%+ GDPC1 growth, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, signaling a tightening monetary cycle, S&P 500 forward returns tend to decline over the next 20 trading days due to increased borrowing costs.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 55% of instances with FEDFUNDS above 4.5%, or walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.01.

mechanism_narrative: Jointly, when UNRATE falls below 4% and PAYEMS increases by 200,000+ in a month, signaling a strong labor market, S&P 500 returns tend to rise over the next 5 trading days due to increased consumer confidence.
evidence_refs: fact:strong labor markets boost consumer spending
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances, or joint proxy Rank IC < 0.05 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 1.5% monthly increase in Industrial Production (INDPRO) indicates supply chain resilience, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as manufacturers' profitability increases.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window, or SPX returns are not significantly higher in months following 1.5%+ INDPRO growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (Retail and Food Services Sales) increases by 1% in a month, indicating strong consumer demand, S&P 500 returns tend to increase over the next 5 trading days as retail sector stocks boost the market.
evidence_refs: fact:retail sales impact consumer discretionary sector
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in > 55% of triggered instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Always, the level of FEDFUNDS inversely correlates with S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as higher rates increase borrowing costs and decrease equity valuations.
failure_condition: Walk-forward correlation coefficient between FEDFUNDS and SPX returns is positive over any 3-year rolling window, or Rank IC < 0.01.

mechanism_narrative: If UNRATE rises by 0.5% in two months, signaling labor market stress, and PAYEMS concurrently shows no growth, S&P 500 returns tend to decline over the next 20 trading days due to decreased consumer confidence.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increase > 0.5% in 2 months and PAYEMS no growth
evidence_refs: fact:labor market stress impacts consumer spending
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances, or joint proxy Rank IC < 0.04 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Always, the level of HOUST (New Privately Owned Housing Starts) positively correlates with S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as new housing construction boosts economic activity and, in turn, equity markets.
failure_condition: Walk-forward correlation coefficient between HOUST and SPX returns is negative over any 2-year rolling window, or Rank IC < 0.02.
